- **Mitigation:** In platform runners, when building the prompt or args for a subagent, use platform_specs or a small adapter (e.g. `subagent_prompt_prefix(platform, subagent_name) -> String`) so that: Cursor => `/subagent_name ` + user prompt; Codex/Claude/Gemini/Copilot => "As <subagent_name>, " + user prompt in system or first message, or omit if platform has no convention. Document in AGENTS.md which platforms support which subagent semantics. Implement the adapter so adding a new platform is a single match arm or config entry.

items.impact: Builders cannot tell whether PM-native child records or provider prompt conventions own delegation semantics, creating provider-specific behavior drift.
items.statement: The delegated contract says provider-native subagent syntax is not normative, and DRY rules prohibit platform match statements, but the mitigation prescribes a Cursor slash-prefix adapter and says a new platform can be added by a match arm or config entry.
items.title: Provider-native subagent syntax is both forbidden and prescribed

evidence.exact_quote: - **Mitigation:** Cache detection per workspace path (cache key: canonical workspace path). Invalidate when the config is reloaded or the workspace path for the run changes. Expose a single entry point (e.g. `get_project_context(workspace) -> Result<ProjectContext>`) that returns cached value if valid. Phase 1/2 implement this; the orchestrator calls that entry point instead of running detection on every tier. Consider a TTL or "cache for the duration of the run" so long sessions don't hold stale data if the user edits the repo.

items.impact: Long runs can select the wrong language/domain worker after repository changes, while aggressive invalidation can repeat expensive scans.
items.statement: The source requires invalidation on config/workspace changes but merely suggests either a TTL or run-duration cache; it does not define file-change invalidation, canonical-path failures, symlink retargeting, multi-project isolation, or which stale result is safe.
items.title: Project-context cache freshness remains an open implementation choice

evidence.exact_quote: - **Mitigation:** **Rule: required wins.** When building the final subagent list: (1) Start from selected list or override list. (2) Add all names in `required_subagents`. (3) Remove any name in `disabled_subagents` unless it is in `required_subagents`. Document this in code and in the Config UI tooltip. In the UI, optionally grey out or hide in the disabled list any name that appears in required.

- **Mitigation:** **Rule: missing or empty override = use auto-selection.** Only a non-empty override list for a tier replaces the selector output. To force no subagents for a tier, the user sets `enable_tier_subagents` false (global) or we add a per-tier "use no subagents" option in a later version. **Implement:** In the orchestrator, if `tier_overrides.get(tier)` is `None` or `Some([])`, use the list from `SubagentSelector::select_for_tier`; otherwise use the override list. Document in code and in the Config tooltip for tier overrides.

items.impact: Prevents divergent final-list construction for two common configuration cases.
items.statement: The source resolves two otherwise ambiguous selection edges: required entries win over disabled entries, and missing or empty overrides preserve auto-selection.
items.title: Required/disabled conflict and empty override semantics are deterministic

evidence.exact_quote: - **Mitigation:** Follow existing Config save behavior: save on explicit Save action and/or mark dirty and prompt on leave. Ensure `use_plan_mode_all_tiers`, `last_per_tier_plan_mode` (if used), and the full `subagent` block (SubagentGuiConfig) are part of the same `GuiConfig` struct and are written in the same `gui_config::save_config()` call from the Config view so we never persist only tier config without plan-mode global or subagent settings. When the user clicks Save on any Config tab, the entire `gui_config` (including these fields) is serialized to the same YAML file.

items.impact: Users can lose settings or persist a mixed old/new configuration while believing the complete GuiConfig was saved.
items.statement: The mitigation does not choose between explicit save, autosave, and dirty-state prompting and does not define atomic write, crash recovery, partial serialization failure, cross-tab concurrency, or rollback behavior.
items.title: Config durability behavior remains 'save and/or prompt'

evidence.exact_quote: - **Force-complete:** If question count exceeds `max + 1` without the agent signaling complete, force-complete the phase:

- **Orchestrator logic:** In `process_ai_turn` (or equivalent), when `parsed.is_phase_complete`, compute current phase question count; if count < min, reject (e.g. send back "Ask at least N questions"); if max is `Some(m)` and count > m, either reject or accept depending on product rule; otherwise accept.

items.impact: The same question count can force completion, reject completion, or accept completion depending on which paragraph an implementer follows.
items.statement: The resolved soft-cap rule force-completes after max+1 and never rejects valid answers, but the later wiring instruction still leaves over-max behavior as 'either reject or accept depending on product rule.'
items.title: Interview max-question transition is both resolved and unresolved

evidence.exact_quote: - **Force-complete:** If question count exceeds `max + 1` without the agent signaling complete, force-complete the phase:

**Wiring:** Add `require_architecture_confirmation: bool` to `InterviewOrchestratorConfig`; set from `gui_config.interview` in `app.rs`. items.impact: A runaway or merely long architecture interview can advance without the explicit confirmation that policy says is mandatory.

evidence.exact_quote: **Wiring:** Add `vision_provider: String` to `InterviewOrchestratorConfig`; set from `gui_config.interview` in `app.rs`. When building requests that include images, use this platform (filtered by platform_specs vision capability). If no image flow exists yet, wire the field and leave the behavior as "use when implementing image/vision flows"; document that in the plan or code.

3. **Runtime use:** In the execution path (orchestrator, phase manager, prompt builder, runner), **read** the field and use it to decide behavior (e.g. min/max question checks, plan_mode, subagent list). No "dead" fields in the execution config.

items.impact: The GUI can persist a preferred vision provider that has no effect while validation still sees the field as present.
items.statement: The plan requires adding a string field and selecting vision-capable requests, but explicitly permits wiring the field without runtime behavior if no image flow exists, contradicting the later no-dead-fields wiring rule and leaving requested/effective provider disclosure absent.
items.title: vision_provider is allowed to remain a dead execution field

evidence.exact_quote: **Rule:** The orchestrator (or a shared validation layer) runs a **config-wiring check at each tier boundary** -- when entering a Phase, when entering a Task, when entering a Subtask, and when entering an Iteration. The check verifies that the config that **should** affect execution at that tier is **present and actually used** (e.g. tier config exists, plan_mode is read from config, interview limits are present in interview config when in interview flow). This catches "built but not wired" even when the checklist is missed.

- **Single validation entry point:** Introduce a function or small module, e.g. `validate_config_wiring_for_tier(tier_type, config_snapshot, context) -> Result<(), WiringError>`. It receives the current tier type (Phase/Task/Subtask/Iteration), the config (or the relevant slice: tier config, interview config, subagent config), and optional context (e.g. "interview run" vs "main run"). It checks the items above for that tier and returns Ok or an error listing what is missing or unused.

items.impact: Built-but-not-wired fields can pass validation merely because they exist in the snapshot, defeating the feature's central purpose.
items.statement: The validator is required to prove that configuration is present and actually used, yet its proposed inputs are only tier type, config snapshot, and context; no runtime-use instrumentation, provenance token, consumed-field trace, or mutation-based test oracle is defined.
items.title: Config-snapshot validator cannot prove a field is actually used

evidence.exact_quote: - **Fail-fast vs warn:** **Recommendation:** Fail fast (return error, log, and surface to user) when a **required** execution-affecting field is missing from the execution config (e.g. tier config for that tier is absent). **Warn** (log and optionally toast) when a field exists in GUI/file config but is not present in the execution config (classic "built but not wired"). This keeps runs from proceeding with wrong config while highlighting wiring gaps without blocking if the product chooses to allow default behavior for optional fields.

items.impact: A run may spawn with absent required config and only a warning, while the UI and receipts can imply verification occurred successfully enough to proceed.
items.statement: The text recommends fail-fast for required execution fields but leaves optional-field defaults to product choice, and the sample exposes a general WarnAndContinue policy even for VerificationStatus::Fail; no non-overridable failure class protects required authority/config invariants.
items.title: Required-field failure can still be warn-and-continue

evidence.exact_quote: - Verification results are persisted as seglog/redb events and projections (`config.validation.*`, `run.qa_cycle_*`, HITL events), not as authoritative ad hoc JSON files.
- **Log verification results:** Log verification results to `.puppet-master/logs/verification.log`

items.impact: Operators can see divergent verification histories, and sensitive findings may escape canonical retention and redaction controls.
items.statement: The lifecycle alignment says verification is persisted as seglog/redb and not authoritative ad hoc JSON, while the responsibility list mandates `.puppet-master/logs/verification.log`; the prologue separately forbids one-off run-history logs, with no projection/diagnostic distinction or retention owner.
items.title: Verification persistence requires both canonical events and a forbidden ad hoc log

evidence.exact_quote: - **UI wiring check (GUI projects):** If `.puppet-master/project/ui/` exists and the current tier node's scope involves UI work, verify that the node's `contract_refs` include at least one wiring matrix entry or command catalog ID. At end-of-tier, re-run the "no unbound UI actions" check against the current state of `ui/wiring_matrix.json` to ensure new interactive elements added during execution are wired.

items.impact: A mislabeled or mixed-scope node can add interactive UI while bypassing the no-unbound-actions check entirely.
items.statement: The UI wiring check is conditional on both directory existence and the node scope involving UI work, but the source does not define the classifier, owner, false-negative behavior, generated/dynamic UI handling, or a required failure when scope metadata is missing.
items.title: UI-scope detection is an unowned bypass point

evidence.exact_quote: - **Mitigation:** (1) Quality over performance: run full checks; do not skip or weaken for speed. Scope quality checks to changed files or this tier's artifacts to stay practical. (2) Define a small canonical quality checklist per tier (e.g. in this plan or verification config): reviewer subagent (required) plus gate criteria (clippy, tests, etc.). (3) Reviewer subagent runs in all three cases: always at end-of-tier, on retry, and when quality gate fails. (4) Unrelated failures (e.g. pre-existing tech debt) are addressed by the parent-tier orchestrator (retry, different subagent, escalate). Reuse existing gates where possible; end verification should call into current gate logic rather than duplicate it.

items.impact: Nested retries and mandatory review can exhaust budgets or deadlock scarce lanes, especially when verification failures recursively trigger more reviewers.
items.statement: The plan requires full checks and a reviewer at every end boundary, retry, and quality failure, but does not reconcile this fan-out with parent budgets, lane capacity, deduplication, cancellation, priority, or behavior when the reviewer itself fails or times out.
items.title: Full boundary verification has no bounded cost or overload behavior
